question.:question/problem:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z=19 \\ 3x+y+2z=31.\end{aligned}
$$
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 & 31\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 & 31\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & -26\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=6 \\ y+2z=13.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=6 \\ y=-2z+13 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2z+13 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).

knowledge_point.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-2y-4z+4w=-2 \\ 2x+y+2z-8w=-5 \\ 2x+2z-10w=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -4 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -8 & -5 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & -10 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -4 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -8 & -5 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & -10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -8 & -5 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & -10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & -12 & -3 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & -10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & -12 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & -14 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & -14 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-2w=-2 \\ y+2w=-5 \\ z-3w=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $w$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ and $z$ in terms of $w$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2w-2 \\ y=-2w-5 \\ z=3w+2 \\ w=w,\end{aligned}
$$

where $w$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z \\ w\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2w-2 \\ -2w-5 \\ 3w+2 \\ w\end{aligned}],\,w\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
